title: The Best Smart Level 2 EV Chargers
subtitle: Wi-Fi home EV chargers with scheduling and charging history, ranked.
intro: We pulled the Level 2 home EV chargers on Amazon and scored them on rating, review volume, and features: amperage, safety certification, and Wi-Fi app control.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

systems_note: Smart EV chargers run in their own apps; none of these listings name Alexa, Google, or Apple Home. Smart Life chargers work with Home Assistant's Tuya integration. All use J1772, so Tesla and other NACS cars need an adapter unless noted.

buyers_guide.a: Plug-in chargers use a NEMA 14-50 outlet and can be moved. Hardwired chargers can deliver more current (48 A or more) and are required for some installs. Both need a 240 V circuit.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: A 40 A charger adds about 30 miles of range per hour on most EVs, which covers overnight charging for nearly everyone. Your car's onboard charger may cap the speed anyway.
Scheduling for cheap off-peak electricity, charging history, and sometimes utility rebates. Check your utility for EV charger rebates before buying.
